sample_shift_note: TAV-01 (Issue #8) sample of the authored tavern shift, authored in docs/tav01_learning_plan.md. These ten records are a representative subset built with the mechanics and props that already exist: six day-1 records that introduce new corpus words (holen, nehmen, zusammen, kosten, billig, teuer, fertig) and four day-2 records that revisit four of them in a changed context. They are NOT the whole shift: the arrival greeting, the order, the bill, the farewell and the drink/service nouns are deferred, because they need props or actions that TAV-03 and TAV-04 have to supply first. The full event list, the deferred lemmas and what each one waits for are written in docs/tav01_learning_plan.md.
event_note: The records are ordered by id and day only. There is no event grouping in the data format yet: scripts/lex01_content.gd presents every record of a day, so one connected shift cannot be expressed as data today. The planned event_id / event_order grouping is described in docs/tav01_learning_plan.md and is deliberately NOT added here, because adding a field the loader ignores would only look like support.
decidability_note: Two rules belong together. (1) A lemma enters target_lemma_ids only if the player has to understand that word to answer: Lex01Progress.attempt() credits every target lemma, so naming a word that the answer does not actually depend on would record practice that never happened. (2) The answer must be workable from facts the scene or the sentence presents: which object is staged where, or a number stated in the utterance itself. t01 and t07 stage one item at the fridge and two on the table, so 'aus dem Kuhlschrank' picks exactly one object. t03 and t10 stage the same two food items together or apart, so the ja/nein answer follows from the scene. t05 and t09 state the rule ('wenn das Broetchen auf dem Tisch ist, ist das Fruehstueck fertig') and stage the fact the rule needs. t04, t06 and t08 give the prices in the utterance, so billig/teuer/kosten are a comparison or a lookup the player can calculate, never a taste or price opinion. t02 decides by object identity, the same basis the committed bring_deliver records use.
deferred_lemma_note: Most new lemmas are NOT targets in this sample and that is deliberate. Bier, Glas, Wein, Wasser, Kaffee, Milch, Rechnung, Speisekarte, Flasche, Essen and Kueche name things with no committed prop model, so a player could read them but never point at them: they wait for TAV-03. bestellen, moechten, gast, danke, 'Wie bitte?', Entschuldigung, zusammen-eating invitations and the greeting depend on social situations that object placement cannot decide, so they wait for the situation ground-truth key and the greeting/order/payment situations in TAV-04. schmecken, wunderbar, gut, hunger, durst, geld, fertig as an adjective of taste need a state the scene cannot represent yet. billig is introduced in t04 and echoed as the wrong sentence in t06, but it has no delayed review here: naming it as reviewed on day 2 would need a task whose answer depends on it, which the bill event (E8) is supposed to be. Making any of these a target now would teach the player to guess.
presentation_note: An option id is the positional label of the authored display order: a = first authored option, b = second, c = third. In this file the correct answers are spread a=5, b=4, c=1, so no position is correct in half or more records - and across all three scenario files the totals stay spread (a=11, b=11, c=5 of 27). LEX-01 still shuffles the visible option order at play time and resolves correctness by option id, never by index.
distractor_note: distractor_lemma_ids = union of the lemma_ids in the incorrect options MINUS the union of the lemma_ids in the correct option, exactly as in the other two scenario files. t03 is a ja/nein pair whose two sentences use the same lemmas, so its list is empty by that rule.
gloss_note: utterance_gloss_ru (and gloss_ru on a respond option) is the short Russian meaning behind the 'Unterschrift · Uebersetzung' hint button, authored by the agent and still needing human review. It is hidden by default and an answer given while it is open counts as assisted. No record here carries guided: true, because LEX-01 already has exactly one guided example (s01).
language_note: German is what the player is learning: utterance_de, option labels and feedback stay German, the interface around them is Russian from data/ui/lex01_ui_ru.json. The Russian glosses here are agent-authored and a human must judge both the German and the Russian wording.
context_note: context names a reusable room layout. 'room' and 'kitchen' are two camera framings of the same tiny preview scene, and the candidate positions differ between them on purpose (data/room/lex01_room.json), so a day-2 revisit is a changed situation instead of a repeated screenshot. Day 1 introduces in kitchen twice and room twice; day 2 revisits those lemmas in the opposite framing.
repetition_note: New lemmas introduced here and reused later in a different role or context: holen (t01 fetch from the fridge in kitchen, t07 same verb with the target and the staged positions swapped in room), kosten (t04 inside a ja/nein judgement in kitchen, t06 inside the same frame with the other item, t08 as the question verb 'was kostet das Broetchen?' in room), billig (t04 as the answer, t06 as the wrong sentence; no day-2 review, see deferred_lemma_note), fertig (t05 answered ja in room, t09 answered nein in kitchen), zusammen (t03 answered nein in kitchen, t10 answered ja in room), broetchen (t02 carried to the table, t04 priced, t03/t10 staged together or apart, t05/t09 the fact the rule is about, t08 the item whose price has to be found), kuehlschrank (t01 the source of the fetch, t03/t09 the place a sentence claims, t07 again the source with a different object).
npc_note: Only the two committed characters exist (der Mage, der Ritter). der Gast is a corpus lemma but has no model, so no record here calls either character a guest; the guest role stays with the existing characters until TAV-03 provides a guest prop, as recorded in docs/tav01_learning_plan.md.

scenarios.utterance_de: Ich habe Hunger. Hol die Tomate aus dem Kühlschrank!
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Я голоден. Достань помидор из холодильника.
scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Danke. Die Tomate ist aus dem Kühlschrank.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Die Tomate ist im Kühlschrank, die Kartoffel liegt auf dem Tisch. Hol die Tomate!
scenarios.notes: Introduces the verb holen by staging the contrast: only the tomato stands at the fridge, the potato and the bun are on the table, so 'aus dem Kuhlschrank' names one object and not a memorised click. 'Ich habe Hunger' and the answer 'Danke' put the noun Hunger and the expression danke in front of the player as words to hear, without claiming either one is learned: der Hunger is not in target_lemma_ids because the scene cannot show hunger.

scenarios.utterance_de: Nimm das Brötchen und bring es auf den Tisch!
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Возьми булочку и отнеси её на стол.
scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Das Brötchen liegt auf dem Tisch. Gut.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Das ist nicht das Brötchen. Nimm das Brötchen und bring es auf den Tisch.
scenarios.notes: Second fetch verb in a different frame: holen in t01 takes something out of a place, nehmen here takes one named thing to a named place. The answer rests on object identity, the same basis the committed bring_deliver records use, and the table is marked as the delivery target.

scenarios.utterance_de: Ist das Brötchen zusammen mit der Tomate auf dem Tisch?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Булочка вместе с помидором на столе?

options.label_de: Ja, das Brötchen ist zusammen mit der Tomate auf dem Tisch.
options.gloss_ru: Да, булочка вместе с помидором на столе.

options.label_de: Nein, das Brötchen ist nicht zusammen mit der Tomate auf dem Tisch.
options.gloss_ru: Нет, булочка не вместе с помидором на столе.

scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Richtig. Das Brötchen ist auf dem Tisch und die Tomate ist im Kühlschrank.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Die Tomate ist im Kühlschrank, nicht auf dem Tisch.
scenarios.notes: Introduces the adverb zusammen. Both sentences carry the same lemmas and differ only by ja/nein and the negation, so distractor_lemma_ids is empty by the documented rule. The answer is visible: the bun is spread on the table and the tomato is staged at the fridge.

scenarios.utterance_de: Das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro. Das Fleisch kostet 8 Euro. Ist das Brötchen billig?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Булочка стоит 1 евро. Мясо стоит 8 евро. Булочка дешёвая?
scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Ja. 1 Euro ist weniger als 8 Euro.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro, das Fleisch kostet 8 Euro.
scenarios.notes: Introduces the verb kosten and the adjective billig with the evidence written into the utterance: two prices, one item named. The player compares numbers the text gives, so cheap/expensive is calculated instead of guessed. teuer appears only in the wrong sentence here and becomes a target in t06.

scenarios.utterance_de: Wenn das Brötchen auf dem Tisch ist, ist das Frühstück fertig. Ist das Frühstück fertig?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Если булочка на столе, завтрак готов. Завтрак готов?

options.label_de: Nein, das Brötchen ist im Kühlschrank.
Ja, das Brötchen ist auf dem Tisch und das Frühstück ist fertig.
options.gloss_ru: Да, булочка на столе и завтрак готов.

scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Ja, das Brötchen liegt auf dem Tisch.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Das Brötchen liegt auf dem Tisch, nicht im Kühlschrank.
scenarios.notes: Introduces fertig without asking the player to judge whether a meal is 'ready': the record states the rule itself and then stages the fact the rule needs, so the answer is the visible position of one object. das Frühstück is not a corpus lemma - it is a verified reserve entry in the vocabulary file - so it can be spoken in an utterance but never carries a lemma id.

scenarios.utterance_de: Das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro. Das Fleisch kostet 8 Euro. Ist das Fleisch teuer?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Булочка стоит 1 евро. Мясо стоит 8 евро. Мясо дорогое?
scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Ja. 8 Euro ist mehr als 1 Euro.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Das Fleisch kostet 8 Euro, das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro.
scenarios.notes: The other half of the t04 frame on the same shift: same two prices, opposite pole, different item named. Repeating a sentence frame while the judged item changes is what keeps the answer from being a memorised option.

scenarios.utterance_de: Hol die Kartoffel aus dem Kühlschrank!
scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Danke. Die Kartoffel ist aus dem Kühlschrank.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Die Kartoffel ist im Kühlschrank, die Tomate liegt auf dem Tisch.
scenarios.notes: Delayed retrieval of holen from t01 with the staged facts swapped: yesterday the tomato was at the fridge and the potato on the table, today it is the other way round, and the framing changes from kitchen to room. The same verb now selects a different object, so the answer cannot be a remembered click.

scenarios.utterance_de: Das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro. Das Fleisch kostet 8 Euro. Was kostet das Brötchen?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Булочка стоит 1 евро. Мясо стоит 8 евро. Сколько стоит булочка?

options.label_de: Das Brötchen kostet 8 Euro, so viel wie das Fleisch.
options.gloss_ru: Булочка стоит 8 евро, столько же, сколько мясо.

scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Ja. Das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro und das Fleisch kostet 8 Euro.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Das Brötchen kostet 1 Euro, 8 Euro kostet das Fleisch.
scenarios.notes: kosten returns on day 2 in a different job than in t04: yesterday the price pair fed a ja/nein judgement about billig, today the question verb itself is what has to be understood - only the sentence carrying the bun's own price is right, and the trap number is the price of the meat that stands next to it. Revised after the PR #14 review: this record was a bring_deliver task ('Bring das Brötchen! Es kostet nur 1 Euro.') whose target_lemma_ids named kosten and billig although the click was decided by the noun Brötchen alone and billig never appeared in the German text at all. Because Lex01Progress.attempt() credits every target lemma, that record would have logged unaided practice of words the player never had to understand. billig is therefore no longer claimed as reviewed here.

scenarios.utterance_de: Wenn das Brötchen auf dem Tisch ist, ist das Frühstück fertig. Ist das Frühstück fertig?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Если булочка на столе, завтрак готов. Завтрак готов?

options.label_de: Ja, das Brötchen ist auf dem Tisch.
Nein, das Brötchen ist im Kühlschrank.

scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Nein, das Brötchen liegt im Kühlschrank. Das Frühstück ist nicht fertig.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Das Brötchen liegt im Kühlschrank.
scenarios.notes: Same rule sentence as t05, opposite facts: the bun is staged at the fridge and the potato on the table, and the framing moves from room to kitchen. Yesterday the answer was ja, today the same words give nein, which is the point of the revisit.

scenarios.utterance_de: Ist das Brötchen zusammen mit der Tomate auf dem Tisch?
scenarios.utterance_gloss_ru: Булочка вместе с помидором на столе?

options.label_de: Ja, das Brötchen ist zusammen mit der Tomate auf dem Tisch.
options.gloss_ru: Да, булочка вместе с помидором на столе.

options.label_de: Nein, die Tomate ist im Kühlschrank.

scenarios.feedback_correct_de: Ja, beide liegen zusammen auf dem Tisch.
scenarios.feedback_wrong_de: Nein. Die Tomate liegt auf dem Tisch.
scenarios.notes: zusammen returns on day 2 with the two objects staged together instead of apart, in the other framing, so the ja/nein answer flips. The wrong sentence names the fridge, which is where the tomato stood yesterday: a plausible alternative, not a random one.
